positioning.category: Environment where agents work: Fawn durable browser workspaces with independently useful GPU execution
positioning.promise: Doe builds the environment where agents work. Fawn provides durable browser workspaces; DoeRuntime supplies independently useful GPU execution; DoeLab tests improvements; DoeProof records evidence. WGSL compilation remains independently usable with separate qualification.
positioning.governingQuestion: Does each selected product preserve its authority and semantics and improve complete user workflows against competent independent controls?
positioning.initialDeploymentStrategy: Hardware-first local execution: the first deployment targets one frozen AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 / Radeon 8060S / RADV workstation, the initial qualification target. Local execution is a deployment strategy, not a mandatory dependency or a universal performance claim; Fawn's goal remains durable browser workspaces, and Doe enters only through explicit integration with independent qualification.

independenceBoundary.rule: Fawn starts above stock Chromium through narrow CDP/Playwright adapters and does not require native runtime wins. The WGSL compiler and native WebGPU runtime can earn adoption independently; neither requires the other or Fawn. Doppler owns model semantics. Chromium hooks and browser-runtime integration are added only when measured benefits justify their compatibility and maintenance costs, and earn separate admission; prepared-program integration remains a separate treatment.

independent semantic oracle, pinned inputs and reproducible installation
separately measured compiler or runtime advantage against the strongest eligible controls
voluntary maintainer adoption and retention across another release or workload
production signer authorization independent of the execution provider

surfaces.job: Provide independently usable WGSL analysis and target lowering. Evaluate compilation latency, diagnostics, supported shader semantics and generated-program performance separately from runtime execution.
surfaces.promotionGate: A concrete external compiler consumer verifies its declared outcome against independent controls and retains use without requiring DoeRuntime. New campaigns need explicit opportunity selection; closed browser transformations stay closed.

surfaces.job: Supply independently useful GPU execution: own WebGPU validation, resources, submission, completion, memory, synchronization and application integration. Runtime adoption does not require independent adoption of the owned compiler.
surfaces.promotionGate: A frozen non-Doppler application demonstrates a material advantage over the strongest eligible controls; declared-program changes are disclosed; external adoption and repeat retention remain independently evidenced.

surfaces.job: Record evidence of provider identity, correctness, fallback, replay, lifecycle, and release admissibility without requiring runtime replacement.
surfaces.promotionGate: Record incumbent and DoeRuntime evidence impartially with independent output validation, provider identity, explicit fallback, and replay; this feature does not itself prove runtime adoption.

surfaces.job: Provide durable browser workspaces where agents work, above Chromium: one shared service for durable authority, versioned observation, trusted action dispatch, recovery and reusable workflow adapters.
surfaces.promotionGate: A shared implemented service passes authority, uncertainty and workflow fault tests and demonstrates complete-task value against competent stock Chromium/Playwright. Documentation, artwork and GPU/browser receipts do not establish workspace acceptance.

surfaces.job: Test improvements offline: turn retained physical failures into minimized reproductions, candidate corrections, and permanent regression gates.
surfaces.promotionGate: A retained field failure produces a reusable qualified correction without weakening evidence or promotion rules.

decisionRules: K0 remains separate from A, B, C, and D because it changes execution location and service architecture rather than one component.
If K0 wins shared tasks and customers assign no value to differentiation, reject the measured shell-product claim; workspace value requires its own competent-baseline evidence.
B must beat A before the legacy Fawn shell build earns standalone value; C must beat B before DoeRuntime earns browser execution; D must beat C before the Direct Protocol survives.

A passing lane is necessary, not sufficient: Chromium hooks, the Direct Protocol and browser-runtime integration are added only when measured benefits justify their compatibility and maintenance costs.
An ineligible K0 row is retained as an eligibility result and never scored as a win for the Fawn workspace or the legacy Fawn shell build.

roadmapProofs.currentStatement: Doe has promising execution evidence; Fawn has scoped workspace advantages. Neither has achieved the final objective.
roadmapProofs.selectionRule: These proofs select current work. Milestone 1 completes within proof 1; milestones 2 and 3 wait until the proofs resolve; proof 3 selects the forced-Doe Chromium build for its comparison only, not for adoption. Correctness repairs, independent installation and technical release are not blocked.

executionOwnership.operatingObjective: Doppler is the first engineering customer. Keep DoeRuntime focused on roadmap proofs 1 and 2: current Doe against Dawn on Vulkan, ending in one correct, reproducible Doppler Node generation advantage, then a current Metal confirmation; ONNX transfer waits. Qualify unchanged Node generation on current Vulkan, diagnose dominant complete-generation costs, and select one general compiler or runtime improvement under frozen acceptance with an independent numerical reference and a competent Dawn control. External recruitment is not an engineering gate. Transfer evidence and voluntary adoption remain separate; existing ONNX distribution is sufficient.
executionOwnership.expansionPrerequisite: Finish each selected Vulkan batch before selecting another. Existing backend regressions do not constitute parallel optimization campaigns. New compiler work needs a concrete opportunity. Expand support through explicit prioritization and separate physical qualification; customer payment is not a prerequisite for technical progress.

provingSet.applicationRule: Unchanged applications and independent correctness references; Doppler exposes inference problems, while another framework establishes independent adoption.
provingSet.measurementRule: Freeze complete-operation scope, primary advantage and regression limits before execution; retain startup, resident costs, responsiveness, uncertainty and raw samples.

developmentEffectiveness.start: Timestamp of a retained reproducible problem with pinned source and inputs.
developmentEffectiveness.stop: Timestamp of independently verified improvement against frozen correctness and application acceptance.
developmentEffectiveness.recordingRule: Record elapsed time and evidence links in existing work records; retain unresolved and rejected attempts separately. No new measurement framework is required.
developmentEffectiveness.engineeringRule: Keep compiler, backends and host adapters independently testable. Reuse, refactoring and agent assistance serve the ordered milestones; avoid abstractions that add execution overhead.
